title: Testing Rate Schedule: Daily Strips Reckoned for a Courtesy Reship
content:
**Schedule.** For a courtesy reship on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program, in place of the tier's not-insulin-treated allowance divided by 90, the strips a day the reship carries are the strips per 30 days on the program's newest written order for test strips divided by 30 when a medical record with purpose over-limit justification is dated within the last above-allowance record recency months of the tier; the tier's insulin-treated allowance divided by 90 for an insulin-treated customer without such a record; and the tier's not-insulin-treated allowance divided by 90 otherwise.

- The strips per 30 days on an order are its units per 30 days times the strips per billing unit; the newest order is the one with the latest order date.
- A record is dated within the last N calendar months when its visit date is later than the same calendar day N months earlier. On a tier whose recency figure is 0 no record falls within it.

| Tier | Record recency, months | Insulin-treated rate without a record | Rate otherwise without a record |
|---|---|---|---|
| Testing Supplies Self-Pay Program | 0 | 1200 divided by 90 | 1200 divided by 90 |
| Testing Supplies Commercial HMO Program | 6 | 450 divided by 90, 5.0 | 150 divided by 90, 1.67 |
| Testing Supplies Commercial PPO Program | 6 | 600 divided by 90, 6.67 | 200 divided by 90, 2.22 |
| Testing Supplies Medicare Advantage Program | 6 | 300 divided by 90, 3.33 | 100 divided by 90, 1.11 |
| Testing Supplies Original Medicare Program | 6 | 300 divided by 90, 3.33 | 100 divided by 90, 1.11 |
| Testing Supplies Medicaid Program | 6 | 450 divided by 90, 5.0 | 100 divided by 90, 1.11 |

**Example (hypothetical).** An over-limit justification record dated 2 months ago and a newest order of 6 units per 30 days give 6 times 50, divided by 30, that is 10 strips a day, whatever the treatment class.
